questions.question: Google evaluates a product page on LCP loading speed, INP responsiveness, and CLS visual stability as ranking signals. What is this metric set called?
questions.explanation: Core Web Vitals — LCP, INP, and CLS — quantify real-user page experience and feed Google's page-experience ranking signal.

questions.question: A pillar guide on 'running shoes' links out to spoke articles on sizing, brands, and marathon training, all interlinked back to it. What SEO structure is this?
questions.explanation: A topic cluster pairs one comprehensive pillar page with interlinked subtopic articles to build topical authority.

questions.question: A product page embeds JSON-LD marking up price, rating, and availability so Google can render rich snippets. Which shared vocabulary does it use?
questions.explanation: Schema.org is the shared structured-data vocabulary search engines read to generate rich results like stars and prices.

questions.question: After a 2011-era Google update, sites built on thin doorway pages and scraped duplicate content lost rankings en masse. Which update was it?
questions.explanation: Panda demoted low-quality, thin, and duplicative content, rewarding original depth.

questions.question: Stores that bought thousands of spammy exact-match anchor backlinks were demoted by which link-quality Google update?
questions.explanation: Penguin targeted manipulative link schemes and over-optimized anchor text, devaluing unnatural backlink profiles.

questions.question: A 500,000-page marketplace finds Googlebot never reaches its deepest faceted pages because it allocates only limited fetch resources per site. What is this limit called?
questions.explanation: Crawl budget is how many URLs a crawler will fetch on a site in a period, bounded by crawl capacity and demand.

questions.question: A React store's pages look blank to crawlers until the fix moves to generating complete HTML on the server for each request. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Server-side rendering executes the app on the server and ships fully formed HTML, so crawlers index content without running JavaScript.

questions.question: An SEO sorts keywords into 'how to tie running shoes' versus 'buy running shoes online' to match content format to the searcher's goal. What is she classifying?
questions.explanation: Search intent — informational, navigational, commercial, or transactional — determines which content type can satisfy a query.

questions.question: A news site must keep comment links working for readers while signaling Google they are not editorial endorsements, adding rel="___" to each. Which value fills the blank?
questions.explanation: rel="nofollow" tells search engines the link is not endorsed, so its ranking weight should not flow to the target.

questions.question: Larry Page's founding algorithm scores a page by counting inbound links as votes, weighted by each voter's own authority. Which algorithm is this?
questions.explanation: PageRank propagates authority through the link graph, treating links as weighted votes for relevance and quality.

questions.question: Google's model reads words bidirectionally, so it finally grasps that 'brazil traveler to usa need a visa' is about going to the US. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: BERT's bidirectional transformer reads full sentence context in both directions, decoding prepositions and nuance in queries.

questions.question: A PDF catalog cannot carry a meta robots tag, so the dev emits the noindex directive through an HTTP response header instead. Which header?
questions.explanation: X-Robots-Tag carries robots directives like noindex and nofollow in HTTP headers, covering non-HTML files such as PDFs.

questions.question: Google must rank a never-before-seen query like 'that shoe store near the mall that closed' by mapping it to known entities with machine learning. Which system is this?
questions.explanation: RankBrain is Google's machine-learning system that generalizes unfamiliar queries onto known intents and entities.

questions.question: A store serves en-PH and en-US variants and must tell Google which regional page to show each audience. Which link attribute signals this?
questions.explanation: hreflang annotations tell search engines each page's language and region so the right variant is served in each market.

questions.question: An SEO says a link from a high-authority domain 'passes juice' that lifts the target page's ranking potential. What is the formal term for that transferred authority?
questions.explanation: Link equity is the ranking value a hyperlink transmits; 'link juice' is the informal nickname for it.

questions.question: Three blog posts on one site all target the phrase best running shoes, and Google ranks none of them well. What is this self-competition called?
questions.explanation: Keyword cannibalization occurs when multiple pages compete for the same query, splitting ranking signals.

questions.question: A store permanently moves /old-shoes to /shoes and wants ranking equity to transfer. Which redirect status code is correct?
questions.explanation: A 301 redirect signals a permanent move and passes most link equity to the new URL.

questions.question: Google predominantly crawls and ranks the mobile version of a site's pages. What is this indexing model called?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first indexing means Google uses the mobile rendition of content for indexing and ranking.

questions.question: Faceted filters generate dozens of URLs for the same product listing. Which link element consolidates signals to the preferred URL?
questions.explanation: rel="canonical" tells search engines which duplicate URL should receive the consolidated ranking signals.

questions.question: In a Lighthouse audit, which Core Web Vitals metric flags page elements jumping around during load?
questions.explanation: Cumulative Layout Shift measures unexpected layout movement; a good score is under 0.1.
